content: The cost of insulin has been steadily increasing over time, creating a significant financial burden for many patients who rely on it for diabetes management. Despite recent efforts to reduce prices, patients continue to face high out-of-pocket expenses, which can negatively impact their ability to adhere to prescribed treatment regimens. In response to these challenges, some states have introduced caps on insulin costs to improve affordability. Additionally, certain manufacturers have announced price reductions as part of their efforts to address the issue of accessibility for patients.
